parameters.name: a
parameters.description: Effective motor acceleration gain multiplying `u`; motor torque constant and inertia are not separately identified.

parameters.name: c
parameters.description: Fundamental sinusoidal restoring acceleration coefficient multiplying `sin(theta)`.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Low-speed damping rate; a numerical regularization parameter, not an independently measured material property.

parameters.name: r
parameters.description: Dimensionless signed bias fraction; its bounds keep the bias inside the static-friction capacity.

parameters.name: h
parameters.description: Dimensionless cosine modulation of friction capacity in `f*(1+h*cos(theta))`; this is an empirical angle-dependent effect, not proof of a specific pad-loading mechanism.

parameters.name: biasAmp
parameters.description: Bounded bias acceleration computed from the fitted friction scale and signed fraction; the tie protects restoring behavior at rest.

estimation.criterion: Sum of squared open-loop angle errors on `theta`, excluding the first sample of each trajectory. Simulations use `dtheta = omega`, classical fourth-order Runge-Kutta, the recorded first `theta` and `omega`, step `T_s = 0.01` s as specified in TASK.md, and zero-order-held `u`. Every scored sample receives equal weight; there are no later state resets. Angle simulation is the intended use and avoids treating differentiated encoder accelerations as noise-free observations.
estimation.data: Final parameter fit: all rows of `data/train.csv` (13 trajectories, 3522 samples) and `data/val.csv` (3 trajectories, 1192 samples), giving 4698 after-initial angle residuals. Validation was first used in structural comparisons and was then reused for calibration; final validation errors are not untouched holdout estimates. A later independent-selection audit, `independent_selection.py`, excludes training trajectories 8 and 11 because they duplicate tails of validation trajectories 1 and 2. Other exact free-response tails are training trajectories 9, 10, 12 and 13, within training trajectories 1, 2, 3 and 4 respectively. They remain separate initial-value simulations because both regimes are requested, but they are not independent experiments.
estimation.method: Bounded nonlinear least squares with the trust-region reflective algorithm, `scipy.optimize.least_squares`, using linear loss, two-point finite differences, `diff_step = 0.0001`, `x_scale = "jac"`, `max_nfev = 500`, `ftol = 1e-9`, `xtol = 1e-9`, and `gtol = 1e-8`. All fitted parameters of this candidate were optimized jointly in one final all-data fit. Initial values were `a = 28.8` rad/(s^2 V); `b = 1.55` 1/s; `c = 114.5` rad/s^2; `f = 29.2` rad/s^2; `k = 180` 1/s; `r = 0.16`; `h = -0.3`; `j = 0`. These rounded trial values came from physically motivated baseline fits and the residual-guided angle-friction comparison; the transition widths were chosen at sub-radian-per-second scales to resolve the low-speed band without an excessively stiff RK4 law. The intermediate derivative initialization used nonnegative linear least squares (`scipy.optimize.lsq_linear`) on moving training rows with `Abs(omega) > 1` rad/s, on the features `u`, `-omega`, `-sin(theta)` and `-sign(omega)`; that initializer requires no start. It was not the final coefficient criterion. The final bounds, in the parameter order above, are recorded in `fit_combined.py` and `results/combined.json`; positive acceleration gains and friction, nonnegative viscous damping, and `-0.8 <= r <= 0.8`, `-0.8 <= h <= 0.8`, `-0.8 <= j <= 0.8` impose the physical safeguards. Optimization is deterministic; no random seed applies. Numba just-in-time compilation accelerates the same RK4 computations. `biasAmp` is computed after fitting by its tie, not separately estimated.

discussion.family: Continuous saturated-force (projected) approximation to static/Coulomb friction, coupled to a nonlinear pendulum. It is a low-speed projection regularization, rather than a discontinuous sign-only Coulomb law. References cited from memory, not verified against a retrieved source: D. Karnopp, Computer Simulation of Stick-Slip Friction in Mechanical Dynamic Systems, Journal of Dynamic Systems, Measurement, and Control (1985); B. Armstrong-Helouvry, P. Dupont and C. Canudas de Wit, A survey of models, analysis tools and compensation methods for the control of machines with friction, Automatica (1994).
discussion.interpretation: The common net applied acceleration is `a*u-b*omega-c*sin(theta)*(1+j*cos(theta))+biasAmp*cos(theta)`: motor actuation, viscous loss, fundamental plus second-harmonic restoring acceleration, and bounded even-angle bias, respectively. The friction capacity is `f*(1+h*cos(theta))`. The cosine capacity and bias terms encode residual angle/direction effects without assigning an unverified mechanical cause. The subtracted friction is `Min(Max(a*u-b*omega-c*sin(theta)*(1+j*cos(theta))+biasAmp*cos(theta)+k*omega,-f*(1+h*cos(theta))),f*(1+h*cos(theta)))`. Outside saturation it is bounded sliding friction; inside saturation `domega = -k*omega`. Thus a continuum of exact rest states exists while low-speed motion decays without sign chatter. For both laws, at `omega = 0` and `u = 0`, the restoring factor satisfies `1+j*cos(theta) > 0`, and `Abs(biasAmp*cos(theta)) < f*(1-Abs(h)) <= f*(1+h*cos(theta))`. Consequently saturation cannot create acceleration away from zero on `-pi <= theta <= pi`, proving R2. Dependence on `u` is a positive gain passed through a nondecreasing dead zone (and, for the blend, a convex mix with the positive sliding gain), proving R3 in the nondecreasing sense. R1 is exact.
discussion.origin: The pre-fit plan is `plan.md`. Motor voltage, viscous damping, sinusoidal restoring torque and Coulomb friction came from physical reasoning, not symbolic regression. Smooth Coulomb, projected stiction, Karnopp dead-band, linear restoring, quadratic damping, cubic motor gain, direction bias, angle-modulated friction, harmonic restoring and Stribeck terms were compared. The linear restoring model simulated poorly; quadratic damping, extra motor nonlinearity and Stribeck excess friction fitted effectively to zero and were omitted. Binned derivative residuals and terminal angle biases motivated the even-angle bias, cosine friction capacity and positive second harmonic. Their forms are low-order empirical guesses constrained to preserve the requirements, not discoveries of individual hardware effects. The projected force saturation replaces an ideal set-valued static friction law with a single-valued expression usable by the required integrator; its advantage is a simple exact stick band. Independent-selection audit RMSE on the three validation trajectories, after excluding the two duplicated training tails, was `0.08963222493299658` rad. Final all-data refit RMSE was `0.047393530590679626` rad on training and `0.0812517225481444` rad on validation. The latter is not a holdout score.
discussion.limitations: Only effective acceleration coefficients are identified: inertia, motor torque constant, gravity torque and physical friction torques cannot be separated. Encoder quantization and differentiation noise limit derivative interpretation. The fitted laws omit electrical and friction-memory states. Trajectories contain repeated experimental tails, and the final fit reuses validation; quoted refit errors are calibration diagnostics, not test predictions. Static endpoints differ between recordings and some terminal errors remain, especially the positive-angle small free release and validation driven trajectory 1. Applicability is limited to this rig and the observed voltages (approximately `-5 <= u <= 4` V on the supplied files), not established over the entire allowed input domain or beyond the observed velocities. No uncertainty interval or extrapolation guarantee is claimed. The projection law is continuous but has derivative corners at saturation boundaries. Its fitted low-speed rate is specific to the required sampling/integration scheme.
